item.title: Incarico post-doc: Nonlinear Analysis and Fragility Assessment of Structures Subjected to Fire and Post-Earthquake Fire (Univ. TRENTO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 12:00
Institution: Univ. TRENTO, Trento
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-07 Tecnica delle costruzioni

The research focuses on the analysis of the behaviour of structures exposed to fire, using advanced fire models and nonlinear thermomechanical analyses. Specifically, the research will investigate the analysis of: - structures in industrial facilities exposed to wildland-urban interface fires and forest fires; - bridge structures exposed to vehicle fires; - structures exposed to fires following earthquake. The development of fragility models will also be required. Finally, support will be required for the nonlinear numerical analysis of the buckling behaviour of tapered webplated steel members.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-10 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milan
Field: Civil engineering and architecture / 08/CEAR-04 Geomatica

Satellite Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) enables monitoring of nonlinear ground deformation with millimetre-level precision and high spatial and temporal resolution. It supports the observation of natural and anthropogenic assets, where slow ground motion may accumulate and lead to subsidence, slope failures, and structural damage. This research addresses the shift from measurement to interpretation and action through: (1) consolidation of InSAR processing schemes; (2) fusion of InSAR products with external data sources across multiple spatial scales; and (3) translation of interpreted deformation into a risk context, enabling retrospective and multi-scenario anticipatory…

The research is based on the idea that each individual component of the built heritage has followed a historical trajectory extending to the present day. Throughout this trajectory, transformations of varying significance have occurred, all interconnected and consequential, either as a coherent continuation or as a more or less conscious rejection of the preceding phase. Each component therefore bears witness to an ongoing process that encompasses, yet extends beyond, the concept of stratigraphy, embracing both tangible and intangible dimensions. Research on the potential offered by production processes, the application of innovative materials, and the adoption of state-of-the-art functional technologies for kitchen appliances and home wellness products. The study will focus on identifying the state of the art and exploring technological and usability trends, with an emphasis on design compatibility regarding existing production processes and product platforms within the sector. The research will be conducted within a multidisciplinary design and engineering framework, encompassing materials engineering, industrial process engineering, and advanced product design.
